directAnswer: Pope Pius II was Enea Silvio Piccolomini of Corsignano near Siena, a celebrated humanist writer and former supporter of the Council of Basel, who reigned from 19 August 1458 to 14 August 1464. He condemned appeals from the pope to a future council, canonized St. Catherine of Siena, rebuilt his birthplace as the town of Pienza, and wrote the Commentaries, the only autobiography written by a reigning pope.

paras: Enea Silvio Piccolomini was born in 1405 at Corsignano, in the territory of Siena, to an impoverished noble family. He studied at Siena and Florence and became known for elegant Latin prose and poetry. He went to the Council of Basel as a secretary, served the antipope Felix V, and later joined the chancery of Emperor Frederick III, who crowned him poet laureate in 1442.

In his early years he wrote secular works, including a popular love story in Latin and a comedy, and he fathered children. In the mid-1440s he reconciled with Eugene IV, was ordained a priest in 1446, and became bishop of Trieste and then of Siena. Callixtus III made him a cardinal in 1456.

sections.h2: Execrabilis and the Retraction of His Conciliarist Past
paras: As pope, Pius defended the authority he had once questioned. In the bull Execrabilis of 1460 he condemned appeals from the pope to a future general council, declaring them void. In 1463, in a bull addressed to the University of Cologne, he retracted his own earlier writings in favor of the council, asking readers to reject the young Aeneas and accept Pius.
He also canonized St. Catherine of Siena in 1461, an act that carried special meaning for a son of Siena.

sections.h2: The Congress of Mantua and the Last Crusade
paras: Pius made a crusade against the Ottoman Turks the chief aim of his reign. In 1459 he summoned Christian rulers to a congress at Mantua, but attendance was poor and pledges were few. A letter addressed to Sultan Mehmed II, inviting him to accept baptism, survives among his writings, though it is uncertain whether it was ever sent.

In 1464 Pius took the cross himself and traveled to Ancona to lead the crusade in person. The promised fleets were slow to arrive, and he died at Ancona on 14 August 1464 before the expedition could depart.

Pius had his birthplace rebuilt by the architect Bernardo Rossellino as a planned Renaissance town, with a cathedral, papal palace and square designed as a unified whole. In 1462 he renamed it Pienza after himself and made it a bishopric. Its center is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

His Commentaries, written in the third person, describe his life, travels, the politics of his time and the landscapes of Italy with unusual vividness. They remain a major source for fifteenth-century history and the only memoir composed by a pope during his reign. His earlier works include descriptions of Germany, Bohemia and Europe.

keyFacts: Born Enea Silvio Piccolomini at Corsignano near Siena in 1405
Humanist author, crowned poet laureate by Frederick III (1442)
Condemned appeals to a future council in Execrabilis (1460)
Rebuilt Corsignano as Pienza (1462) and wrote the Commentaries
Died at Ancona on 14 August 1464 while preparing a crusade

faqs.question: What are the Commentaries of Pius II?
faqs.answer: They are his memoirs, written in the third person during his pontificate. They describe his life and times in detail and are the only autobiography written by a reigning pope.

faqs.question: Why did Pius II retract his earlier writings?
faqs.answer: As a young man at the Council of Basel he had argued that a general council was superior to the pope. As pope he publicly withdrew those views in 1463, asking readers to reject Aeneas and accept Pius.

faqs.question: What is Pienza?
faqs.answer: It is his birthplace, Corsignano, which he had rebuilt as an ideal Renaissance town by Bernardo Rossellino and renamed Pienza in 1462.
